text:
Fierce spring! My tenderness goes

spilled through the deepest veins,

fresh fountainhead, and wakeful fury,

hurrying toward exhausting amazement.


Oh what panting, what boiling, oh, what haste

to find, in the closed hill,

the red wound of the frozen cave,

and its sweetest cure, in madness!


Fleeting monster, terror of my life,

lightless lightning, oh you, my spring,

my fierce beast, my strong archangel!


Toward what shadowy depth does your hair,

unfurled and astral, invite me?

Love, love, beginning of death!

translation.title: Love
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps love as both spring-force and deathward terror, preserving the poem's erotic and apocalyptic force.
